business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K MD&A Key Performance Indicators section
business_model.claim: Key performance indicators that drive Hospitality revenue are hotel occupancy (volume), average daily rate (price), RevPAR, Total RevPAR, and net definite room nights booked.
quotes: hotel occupancy – a volume indicator; average daily rate ("ADR") – a price indicator calculated by dividing rooms revenue by the number of rooms sold; revenue per available room ("RevPAR") – a summary measure of hotel results calculated by dividing rooms revenue by room nights available to guests for the period; total revenue per available room ("Total RevPAR") – a summary measure of hotel results calculated by dividing the sum of room, food and beverage and other ancillary service revenue by room nights available to guests for the period; and net definite room nights booked – a volume indicator which represents the total number of definite bookings for future room nights at our hotels confirmed during the applicable period, net of cancellations.

business_model.claim: The company pays Marriott base management fees of approximately 2% to 3.5% of gross revenues per property plus incentive management fees based on hotel profitability; in 2025, base management fees were $50.8 million and incentive management fees were $27.4 million.
quotes: The applicable percentage for our Gaylord Hotels properties, excluding Gaylord Rockies, is approximately 2% of gross revenues, Gaylord Rockies and JW Marriott Desert Ridge are approximately 3% of gross revenues, and JW Marriott Hill Country is approximately 3.5% of gross revenues.
We incurred $50.8 million, $46.7 million and $41.3 million in base management fees to Marriott related to our Hospitality segment during 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

business_model.claim: The company's operational risk is concentrated in Marriott, which manages all current hotel properties and generates substantially all Hospitality segment revenue.
quotes: Our current hotel properties, the operation of which generates substantially all our Hospitality segment revenue, are operated and managed by Marriott. As a result, our operational risk is concentrated in one third-party hotel manager, which makes us more vulnerable economically to any weakness of Marriott than if we entered into hotel management agreements with several third-party hotel managers.

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 and Risk Factors
business_model.claim: The company's dividend policy requires minimum dividends of 100% of REIT taxable income annually, limiting retained earnings available to fund acquisitions or capital improvements.
quotes: Our dividend policy provides that we will make minimum dividends of 100% of REIT taxable income annually, subject to our board of directors' future determinations as to the amount of any distributions and the timing thereof.

We may not be able to fund capital improvements or acquisitions solely from cash provided from our operating activities because we must distribute at least 90% of our REIT taxable income (determined before the deduction for dividends paid and net of capital gains) each year to maintain our qualification as a REIT for federal income tax purposes.

The Company completed the acquisition of the 1,592-room Grande Lakes Orlando Resort ("Grande Lakes Orlando") on September 1, 2026, adding a turnkey asset in the nation's top meetings market(2) and creating incremental group customer rotation opportunities.

risks.basis: stated in P2 and P5 as an explicit risk factor
risks.claim: Ryman's entire hotel portfolio operates under brands owned by a single third-party manager, Marriott, creating concentrated brand and management risk.
quotes: Our current hotel properties, the operation of which generates substantially all our Hospitality segment revenue, are operated and managed by Marriott. As a result, our operational risk is concentrated in one third-party hotel manager, which makes us more vulnerable economically to any weakness of Marriott than if we entered into hotel management agreements with several third-party hotel managers.

Each of our Gaylord Hotels properties, JW Marriott Hill Country, JW Marriott Desert Ridge and Grande Lakes Orlando operate under a brand owned by Marriott; therefore, we are subject to risks associated with concentrating our hotel portfolio in brands owned by Marriott.
